text:
maya: customer reports intermittent 429s and higher tail latency around 14:00-14:20 UTC. asking for repro evidence (request IDs, headers, HAR/curl, timeline).

devon: thanks — can you grab a few request IDs from the responses (header name usually x-request-id or x-rw-request-id) and timestamps in UTC? also need a full response header dump and one curl that reproduces a 429.

maya: customer sent two sample request ids: rq_20260317_8a1f and rq_20260317_8a2b. they attached a tiny log snippet.

maya: ```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Date: Thu, 17 Mar 2026 14:05:12 GMT
Content-Type: application/json
x-request-id: rq_20260317_8a1f
x-rate-limit-limit: 120
x-rate-limit-remaining: 0
x-rate-limit-reset: 161
Retry-After: 2
{ "error": "quota_exceeded" }
```

sam: good, that looks like a quota window. please also collect a HAR from the client if possible (Chrome DevTools -> Export HAR). HAR shows timing and whether bursts are client-side.

devon: if customer can't grab HAR, ask them to run this curl to capture headers + body: 

```bash
curl -i -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
  -H "x-request-id: test-rq-$(date +%s)" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate \
  -d '{"input":"hello"}' \
  --trace-ascii curl_trace.txt
# attach curl_trace.txt and the response headers
```

devon: alternative to reproduce burst locally (small bash loop) — useful to show pattern: 

```bash
for i in {1..40}; do 
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" -H "x-request-id: local-$i" \
    https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate -d '{"input":"hi"}' &
  sleep 0.2
done
wait
```

arjun: note — include client region, SDK version, and whether they're using streaming. streaming can hold open connections and affect quota accounting on some tiers.

maya: customer replied: they're using SDK v0.9.2 from eu-west-1, non-streaming, running from a scheduled job every minute. they said the job sometimes spikes and coincides with 429s.

sam: perfect. ask them to run the bash loop above but with a slower cadence first (sleep 1) and share timings. we want to know if it's a short burst that crosses the per-second burst threshold or a sustained higher QPS.

maya: asking customer to attach full debug bundle. suggested command we sent them to collect system info and SDK logs: 

```bash
# run on machine where issue happens
mkdir -p /tmp/redwood-debug && cd /tmp/redwood-debug
env > env.txt
ps aux > procs.txt
# capture one example request/response
curl -i -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" -H "x-request-id: dbg-$(date +%s)" \
  https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate -d '{"input":"debug"}' --trace-ascii curl_trace.txt
# package logs
tar czf redwood-debug-$(date +%s).tgz env.txt procs.txt curl_trace.txt /var/log/redwood_sdk.log || true
# then upload to secure bucket and paste link
```

ops-bot: debug bundle upload detected: https://redwood-internal/upload/DBG-9876 (uploaded by customer) :eyes:

devon: pulling the bundle now. if we see many overlapping connections with identical x-request-id prefixes, that's a client retry loop causing bursts. also check the x-rate-limit-* headers timeline — attach a CSV of timestamp, x-request-id, remaining, reset if you can.

maya: customer attached HAR and the tarball. HAR shows 30 concurrent requests in a 10s window starting 14:04:55 UTC.

arjun: that matches a burst. suggest short-term mitigation: add jitter to scheduled job, or rate-limit on client side to keep under 50 QPS per API key for their Dedicated plan. also recommend using retry-backoff with exponential jitter.

sam: i've created internal ticket RID-2345 to correlate backend logs and confirm quota model behavior. adding eng-sre for trace.

devon: next steps for customer: 1) run the curl --trace command once to give us a request/response with headers, 2) if they can, run the controlled bash loop and re-upload trace, 3) confirm whether they can shift schedule by 30s to smooth bursts. we'll check the backend counters for rq_20260317_8a1f and rq_20260317_8a2b.

maya: customer acknowledged and will run the test in the next 30 minutes. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: ticket RID-2345 assigned to devon, priority P2.
